Prosphora

Bake the bread

Learning the tradition of prosphora.

The bread offered for the Divine Liturgy does not simply appear on Sunday morning. Members of our parish prepare and offer prosphora for the celebration of the Eucharist, and they were all taught by somebody.

If you would like to learn, Presbytera offers prosphora-baking classes teaching our parish's own practice and requirements. After learning to prepare prosphora the way this parish does it, parishioners can ask about joining the baking rotation.

It is not a difficult thing to learn. It is a particular thing to learn, which is not the same, and it is why the class comes first.

Three steps, in order

Learn to bake prosphora → Ask about joining the rotation → View the baking schedule →

The first leads to the interest list for parish classes. The other two are inert: joining the rotation is arranged with the parish, not through a form, and there is no schedule to show yet.

The baking schedule

So that approved bakers know who is baking each week, which Sundays are still open, and when their own turn comes.

Sunday Baker

No schedule has been published yet. When there is one, it will appear here — no dates and no names have been invented to fill the space.

Not an open sign-up — by design

If the parish teaches its own practice before somebody bakes for the Liturgy, then a public sign-up button would quietly route around the teaching. So the rotation is asked about rather than joined, and how the parish wants that approval handled is Fr. John and Presbytera's decision to make.

Everything on this card is proposed. Whether the classes run, who teaches them and how a baker is added to the rotation all have to be confirmed before any of it is published.
